<part id="part-mvg3bxd9b732b7" title="2.1 Obligations">
<paragraph id="b7" number="§2.1">
<now>The Recipient shall: (a) keep the Discloser's Confidential Information confidential; (b) use it only for the Purpose; and (c) not disclose it to any person except its and its Affiliates' employees, officers, professional advisers and subcontractors who need to know it for the Purpose and who are bound by confidentiality obligations no less protective than those in this Agreement.</now>
<their_changes>
<change index="1" type="insertion" by="Brightwater Legal">and its Affiliates' </change>
</their_changes>
</paragraph>
<finding id="f-mvg3c18q1d94c4" check="intent" severity="high" paragraph="b7">Differs from our approved “Confidentiality obligations”: The contract adds 'and its Affiliates' before 'employees, officers, professional advisers and subcontractors', allowing disclosure to Affiliates' personnel. The approved clause does not include Affiliates. (favours them)</finding>
<finding id="f-mvg3c18q005684" check="standards" severity="warn" paragraph="b7">Wording to fix it: Removes the unapproved reference to Affiliates, aligning with our standard clause.
Suggested wording: The Recipient shall: (a) keep the Discloser's Confidential Information confidential; (b) use it only for the Purpose; and (c) not disclose it to any person except its employees, officers, professional advisers and subcontractors who need to know it for the Purpose and who are bound by confidentiality obligations no less protective than those in this Agreement.</finding>
<finding id="f-mvg3c1ah3a2c02" check="their-change" severity="warn" paragraph="b7">Recommend rejecting their change: The insertion introduces the undefined term 'Affiliates', which is not defined anywhere in the contract. This creates ambiguity about which entities are covered, potentially leading to disputes over the scope of permitted disclosure. The term should be defined or the change should be rejected.
Recommendation: reject their change 1</finding>
<finding id="f-mvg3c1ah958350" check="language" severity="warn" paragraph="b7">Language: The term 'Affiliates' is not defined in the contract, making the scope of permitted disclosees unclear. Suggested: Either define 'Affiliates' in the definitions section or remove the insertion.</finding>
</part>

<part id="part-mvg3bxd95d61b4" title="2.2 Standard of Care">
<paragraph id="b8" number="§2.2">
<now>The Recipient must protect the Discloser's Confidential Information with no less than the degree of care it applies to its own confidential information and, in any event, with at least reasonable care.</now>
<their_changes>
<change index="1" type="deletion">shall </change>
<change index="2" type="insertion">must </change>
<change index="4" type="deletion">using at least the same </change>
<change index="5" type="insertion">with no less than the </change>
<change index="7" type="deletion">uses to protect </change>
<change index="8" type="insertion">applies to </change>
<change index="10" type="deletion">information, and in any event no less than </change>
<change index="11" type="insertion">information and, in any event, with at least </change>
</their_changes>
</paragraph>
<finding id="f-mvg3c18t061aba" check="their-change" severity="warn" paragraph="b8">Recommend accepting their change: Replacing 'shall' with 'must' is a stylistic change with no substantive difference; both impose an obligation.
Recommendation: accept their change 1</finding>
<finding id="f-mvg3c18t9aeca5" check="their-change" severity="warn" paragraph="b8">Recommend accepting their change: 'with no less than the' is equivalent to 'using at least the same' and is slightly more precise.
Recommendation: accept their change 2</finding>
<finding id="f-mvg3c18t887388" check="their-change" severity="warn" paragraph="b8">Recommend accepting their change: The rephrasing 'and, in any event, with at least' preserves the original meaning and improves readability.
Recommendation: accept their change 4</finding>
</part>

<part id="part-mvg3bxd9cdabdd" title="2.4 Residuals">
<paragraph id="b10" number="§2.4">
<now>Notwithstanding clause 2.1, either party shall be free to use for any purpose the Residuals resulting from access to or work with the Confidential Information of the other party. "Residuals" means information in non-tangible form which may be retained in the unaided memory of persons who have had access to the Confidential Information.</now>
<their_changes>
<change index="0" type="insertion" by="Brightwater Legal">Notwithstanding clause 2.1, either party shall be free to use for any purpose the Residuals resulting from access to or work with the Confidential Information of the other party. "Residuals" means information in non-tangible form which may be retained in the unaided memory of persons who have had access to the Confidential Information.</change>
</their_changes>
</paragraph>
<finding id="f-mvg3c1aj34ed3e" check="intent" severity="high" paragraph="b10">Differs from our approved “Confidentiality obligations”: Clause 2.4 overrides clause 2.1 with 'Notwithstanding', allowing use of Residuals for any purpose, whereas the approved obligations clause requires use only for the Purpose. (favours them)</finding>
<finding id="f-mvg3c1aj57e7cb" check="standards" severity="warn" paragraph="b10">Wording to fix it: The original clause is unacceptable because it allows use of Residuals for any purpose, undermining confidentiality. The replacement clarifies that no such use is permitted, aligning with clause 2.1 and our standard.
Suggested wording: For the avoidance of doubt, neither party shall use any Confidential Information, including information retained in the unaided memory of its personnel, for any purpose other than the Purpose.</finding>
<finding id="f-mvg3c1c2eed741" check="conflict" severity="high" paragraph="b10">Conflicts with another clause: Clause 2.4 overrides clause 2.1 (b7) by permitting use of Residuals for any purpose, undermines the protection standard in clause 2.2 (b8) by exempting Residuals from the required care, and conflicts with clause 3.2 (b13) which grants no licence except for the Purpose.</finding>
<finding id="f-mvg3c1c2f6d10a" check="their-change" severity="warn" paragraph="b10">Recommend rejecting their change: The inserted clause 2.4 creates a broad exception that conflicts with clause 3.2 (b13) and undermines the confidentiality obligations in clauses 2.1 (b7) and 2.2 (b8). The definition of 'Residuals' is vague and could be interpreted to include trade secrets, which would significantly weaken the protection intended by the agreement. The clause should be removed or substantially narrowed to align with the rest of the contract.
Recommendation: reject their change 0</finding>
<finding id="f-mvg3c1c2c66119" check="language" severity="warn" paragraph="b10">Language: The definition of 'Residuals' is ambiguous: 'information in non-tangible form which may be retained in the unaided memory' is unclear and could encompass a wide range of information, including trade secrets, without clear boundaries. Suggested: Consider clarifying the definition to exclude trade secrets or to require that Residuals not be used in a way that competes with the Discloser's business.</finding>
</part>

<part id="part-mvg3bxd9e42421" title="3.3 No Warranty">
<paragraph id="b14" number="§3.3">
<now></now>
<as_they_sent_it>(deleted by them)</as_they_sent_it>
<their_changes>
<change index="0" type="deletion" by="Brightwater Legal">Confidential Information is provided "as is". The Discloser gives no warranty as to its accuracy or completeness.</change>
</their_changes>
</paragraph>
<finding id="f-mvg3c1c03229a2" check="their-change" severity="warn" paragraph="b14">Recommend rejecting their change: The deletion removes clause 3.3, which disclaims any warranty as to the accuracy or completeness of Confidential Information. This is a protective provision for the discloser (PortSwigger). Without it, the discloser could be exposed to claims that the information provided was inaccurate or incomplete, as no other clause in the agreement provides such a disclaimer. The deletion is not necessary for consistency and would undermine the discloser's protection.
Recommendation: reject their change 0</finding>
</part>

<part id="part-mvg3bxd90d6ef7" title="4.1 Term">
<paragraph id="b16" number="§4.1">
<now>This Agreement starts on the date of last signature and continues for two (2) years. The obligations in this Agreement shall continue for five (5) years from the date of termination or expiry, except in relation to trade secrets, which shall be protected for as long as they remain trade secrets.</now>
<their_changes>
<change index="1" type="deletion" by="Brightwater Legal">three (3)</change>
<change index="2" type="insertion" by="Brightwater Legal">five (5)</change>
</their_changes>
</paragraph>
<finding id="f-mvg3c1dla23fbe" check="standards" severity="warn" paragraph="b16">Wording to fix it: No change needed; acceptable as is.
Suggested wording: This Agreement starts on the date of last signature and continues for two (2) years. The obligations in this Agreement shall continue for five (5) years from the date of termination or expiry, except in relation to trade secrets, which shall be protected for as long as they remain trade secrets.</finding>
<finding id="f-mvg3c1f441056a" check="their-change" severity="warn" paragraph="b16">Recommend accepting their change: The deletion of 'three (3)' is part of a single modification that increases the survival period for confidentiality obligations from three to five years. This is a reasonable and common duration for an NDA, provides better protection for confidential information, and does not conflict with any other clause in the agreement.
Recommendation: accept their change 1</finding>
<finding id="f-mvg3c1f42bad53" check="their-change" severity="warn" paragraph="b16">Recommend accepting their change: The insertion of 'five (5)' replaces the previous three-year survival period with a five-year period. This is consistent with the mutual nature of the agreement and does not undermine or override any other provision. It is a standard duration for such obligations and is favourable to both parties' interests in protecting confidential information.
Recommendation: accept their change 2</finding>
<finding id="f-mvg3c1f4cddf91" check="language" severity="warn" paragraph="b16">Language: The clause refers to 'obligations in this Agreement' without specifying which obligations, which could be ambiguous. However, this ambiguity is pre-existing and not introduced by the proposed change. Suggested: Consider clarifying which obligations are intended to survive, e.g., by referring to 'the obligations in clauses 2 and 3' or similar.</finding>
<finding id="f-mvg3c1f41c64fa" check="language" severity="warn" paragraph="b16">Language: The term 'trade secrets' is not defined in the agreement, which could lead to uncertainty about what qualifies. This is a pre-existing issue and not affected by the change. Suggested: Consider adding a definition of 'trade secrets' or referencing applicable law.</finding>
</part>

<part id="part-mvg3bxd961f2c2" title="5.4 Assignment">
<paragraph id="b21" number="§5.4">
<now>Neither party may assign or transfer this Agreement without the prior written consent of the other party, except that either party may assign this Agreement to a member of its group or to a successor to all or substantially all of its business.</now>
<their_changes>
<change index="1" type="deletion">such consent not to be unreasonably withheld, </change>
</their_changes>
</paragraph>
<finding id="f-mvg3c1dm583b99" check="their-change" severity="warn" paragraph="b21">Recommend rejecting their change: The deletion removes the requirement that consent to assignment not be unreasonably withheld. This would allow either party to arbitrarily block assignment, which is a standard protection in mutual agreements. Retaining the reasonableness standard ensures fairness and reduces the risk of disputes. The change is not necessary and would weaken the clause for both parties.
Recommendation: reject their change 1</finding>
</part>

<part id="part-mvg3bxd9abcfea" title="5.8 Governing Law">
<paragraph id="b25" number="§5.8">
<now>This Agreement and any dispute or claim arising out of or in connection with it shall be governed by the laws of the State of New York.</now>
<their_changes>
<change index="1" type="deletion" by="Brightwater Legal">law </change>
<change index="2" type="insertion" by="Brightwater Legal">laws of the State </change>
<change index="4" type="deletion" by="Brightwater Legal">England and Wales.</change>
<change index="5" type="insertion" by="Brightwater Legal">New York.</change>
</their_changes>
</paragraph>
<finding id="f-mvg3c1f5384ca7" check="intent" severity="high" paragraph="b25">Differs from our approved “Governing law”: The clause specifies the laws of the State of New York instead of the law of England and Wales. (favours them)</finding>
<finding id="f-mvg3c1f5540584" check="standards" severity="warn" paragraph="b25">Wording to fix it: Matches our standard position and approved clause.
Suggested wording: <now>This Agreement and any dispute or claim arising out of or in connection with it shall be governed by the law of England and Wales, and the courts of England and Wales shall have exclusive jurisdiction.</now></finding>
<finding id="f-mvg3cmswfe1626" check="conflict" severity="warn" paragraph="b25">Conflicts with another clause: The governing law clause (5.8) now selects New York law, but the contract identifies PortSwigger as a company registered in England and Wales and the signature block references PortSwigger Ltd. This creates a conflict with the parties' apparent domicile and the likely expectation of English law, though it does not directly contradict a specific clause.</finding>
<finding id="f-mvg3cmsw3a21a2" check="their-change" severity="warn" paragraph="b25">Recommend rejecting their change: Deleting 'law' and inserting 'laws of the State' is a stylistic change that does not alter meaning. However, it is part of a package that changes the governing law from England and Wales to New York, which is a substantive change. If the intent is to keep English law, reject the whole package; if the intent is to change to New York, accept this stylistic change as part of that.
Recommendation: reject their change 1</finding>
<finding id="f-mvg3cmsw551f96" check="their-change" severity="warn" paragraph="b25">Recommend rejecting their change: This insertion changes the governing law to New York, which conflicts with the parties' English/UK context (PortSwigger is an English company). Unless there is a strong commercial reason, this should be rejected to maintain consistency with the parties' domicile and the rest of the contract's UK-oriented provisions (e.g., clause 5.6 referencing the UK Contracts (Rights of Third Parties) Act 1999).
Recommendation: reject their change 2</finding>
<finding id="f-mvg3cmsw43732a" check="their-change" severity="warn" paragraph="b25">Recommend rejecting their change: Deleting 'England and Wales' removes the original governing law, which is consistent with the parties' English/UK context. This change, combined with the insertion of New York, is a substantive alteration that should be rejected unless a change to New York law is explicitly desired.
Recommendation: reject their change 4</finding>
<finding id="f-mvg3cmswdb88ee" check="their-change" severity="warn" paragraph="b25">Recommend rejecting their change: Inserting 'New York' as the governing law conflicts with the contract's UK-oriented elements (e.g., clause 5.6 referencing UK legislation, and the parties' English/UK domicile). This should be rejected to avoid inconsistency and potential enforceability issues.
Recommendation: reject their change 5</finding>
<finding id="f-mvg3cmsw729823" check="language" severity="warn" paragraph="b25">Language: The clause as amended is clear in selecting New York law, but it is inconsistent with the contract's UK context, particularly clause 5.6 which references the UK Contracts (Rights of Third Parties) Act 1999. This creates a potential conflict in interpretation, as the contract would be governed by New York law but contains a UK-specific statutory reference. Suggested: If New York law is to be adopted, consider amending or removing clause 5.6 to avoid inconsistency. If English law is preferred, reject the changes.</finding>
</part>

<part id="part-mvg3bxd95a0bb8" title="5.9 Jurisdiction">
<paragraph id="b26" number="§5.9">
<now>The state and federal courts located in New York County, New York shall have exclusive jurisdiction to settle any dispute or claim arising out of or in connection with this Agreement.</now>
<their_changes>
<change index="1" type="insertion" by="Brightwater Legal">state and federal </change>
<change index="3" type="deletion" by="Brightwater Legal">of England and Wales </change>
<change index="4" type="insertion" by="Brightwater Legal">located in New York County, New York </change>
</their_changes>
</paragraph>
<finding id="f-mvg3c1gmdbcb3c" check="intent" severity="high" paragraph="b26">Differs from our approved “Jurisdiction”: The clause specifies exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts in New York County, New York, whereas the approved clause specifies exclusive jurisdiction of the courts of England and Wales. (favours them)</finding>
<finding id="f-mvg3c1gm2775ca" check="standards" severity="warn" paragraph="b26">Wording to fix it: Aligns with our standard governing law and jurisdiction position.
Suggested wording: The courts of England and Wales shall have exclusive jurisdiction to settle any dispute or claim arising out of or in connection with this Agreement.</finding>
<finding id="f-mvg3c1i47b78aa" check="their-change" severity="warn" paragraph="b26">Recommend accepting their change: The insertion of 'state and federal' clarifies that both state and federal courts have jurisdiction, which is consistent with the governing law clause 5.8 (New York law) and does not conflict with any other provision.
Recommendation: accept their change 1</finding>
<finding id="f-mvg3c1i41cd48f" check="their-change" severity="warn" paragraph="b26">Recommend accepting their change: The insertion of 'located in New York County, New York' specifies the venue for the exclusive jurisdiction, which is consistent with the governing law clause 5.8 and does not conflict with any other provision.
Recommendation: accept their change 3</finding>
</part>

<part id="part-mvg3bxd9f532f3" title="5.10 Non-Solicitation">
<paragraph id="b27" number="§5.10">
<now>Non-solicitation. During the term of this Agreement and for twenty-four (24) months after it ends, PortSwigger shall not directly or indirectly solicit, employ or engage any employee of Brightwater with whom it has had contact in connection with the Purpose.</now>
<their_changes>
<change index="0" type="insertion" by="Brightwater Legal">Non-solicitation. During the term of this Agreement and for twenty-four (24) months after it ends, PortSwigger shall not directly or indirectly solicit, employ or engage any employee of Brightwater with whom it has had contact in connection with the Purpose.</change>
</their_changes>
</paragraph>
<finding id="f-mvg3ck7b9ec3f5" check="intent" severity="high" paragraph="b27">Differs from our approved “Confidentiality obligations”: The approved clause is a mutual confidentiality obligation. The part under review is a one-way non-solicitation restriction on PortSwigger only, which is a different subject matter entirely. (favours them)</finding>
<finding id="f-mvg3ck7b3b603f" check="standards" severity="warn" paragraph="b27">Wording to fix it: This makes the clause mutual, reduces the term to 12 months, and adds the required carve-out for general job advertisements, aligning with the acceptable fallback in our standard position.
Suggested wording: Non-solicitation. During the term of this Agreement and for twelve (12) months after it ends, neither party shall directly or indirectly solicit, employ or engage any employee of the other party with whom it has had contact in connection with the Purpose, provided that this clause shall not prevent either party from advertising generally for staff or from employing any person who responds to such an advertisement.</finding>
<finding id="f-mvg3cy2ydcfbae" check="their-change" severity="warn" paragraph="b27">Recommend rejecting their change: The change is a new insertion of a one-sided non-solicitation clause that only restricts PortSwigger, not Brightwater. This is inconsistent with the mutual nature of the agreement (e.g., clause 1.1, 2.1, 2.2, 3.1, 3.2, 5.1, 5.4, 5.5, 5.7, 5.8, 5.9 all apply to both parties). It also conflicts with clause 5.4's assignment provision, as it does not bind assignees, and it is not balanced or reciprocal. <part id="part-mvg3vf2m8e10c9" title="Definition: Confidential Information">
<paragraph id="b4" number="Section 1.01">
<now>"Confidential Information" means any non-public information, in whatever form, disclosed by a Party (the "Disclosing Party") or its Representatives to the other Party (the "Receiving Party") or its Representatives, whether before or after the Effective Date, including technical, financial, commercial and product information, and any information marked as confidential or that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential.</now>
</paragraph>
<finding id="f-mvg3vwpc1f7fa2" check="standards" severity="warn" paragraph="b4">Wording to fix it: Aligns exactly with our approved clause, removing the slight differences in wording (e.g. 'any non-public information' vs 'all information of a confidential nature').
Suggested wording: <now>"Confidential Information" means all information of a confidential nature disclosed by or on behalf of one party (the "Disclosing Party") to the other party (the "Receiving Party"), whether before or after the Effective Date, in any form, including business, technical, financial and product information, and any information that is marked as confidential or would reasonably be regarded as confidential.</now></finding>
</part>

<part id="part-mvg3vf2m28a8bc" title="Section 2.01 – Confidentiality obligations">
<paragraph id="b8" number="Section 2.01">
<now>The Receiving Party shall (a) hold the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information in confidence, (b) use it solely to evaluate and pursue the Transaction, and (c) disclose it only to those of its Representatives who need to know it for that purpose and who are under obligations of confidentiality at least as protective as this Agreement. The Receiving Party is responsible for any breach of this Agreement by its Representatives.</now>
</paragraph>
<finding id="f-mvg3w89nf8c01b" check="standards" severity="warn" paragraph="b8">Wording to fix it: The wording is substantively equivalent to our approved clause. The only difference is the broader definition of Representatives (which includes Affiliates, agents, consultants and financing sources). If we want to narrow it, we could replace 'Representatives' with 'employees, officers, professional advisers and subcontractors' and delete the reference to Affiliates, but that would require amending the definition in Section 1.02. Given the mutual nature and the fact that the disclosure is limited to those who need to know for the Transaction, this is acceptable.
Suggested wording: <now>The Receiving Party shall (a) hold the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information in confidence, (b) use it solely to evaluate and pursue the Transaction, and (c) disclose it only to those of its Representatives who need to know it for that purpose and who are under obligations of confidentiality at least as protective as this Agreement. The Receiving Party is responsible for any breach of this Agreement by its Representatives.</now></finding>
</part>

<part id="part-mvg3vf2m330216" title="Section 2.02 – Exclusions">
<paragraph id="b9" number="Section 2.02">
<now>The obligations in Section 2.01 do not apply to information that the Receiving Party can show (a) is or becomes generally available to the public other than through a breach of this Agreement, (b) was lawfully known to it before receipt from the Disclosing Party, (c) is received from a third party who is not under a duty of confidentiality, or (d) is independently developed without use of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.</now>
</paragraph>
<finding id="f-mvg3w25868e997" check="standards" severity="warn" paragraph="b9">Wording to fix it: Aligns the third-party exclusion with our approved wording, which is broader and more protective of the Receiving Party.

</part>

<part id="part-mvg3vf2m4746b6" title="Section 2.05 – Residual knowledge">
<paragraph id="b12" number="Section 2.05">
<now>Nothing in this Agreement shall restrict either Party from using, for any purpose, any information retained in the unaided memory of its Representatives who had access to Confidential Information, including ideas, concepts, know-how and techniques contained therein.</now>
</paragraph>
<finding id="f-mvg3wmtacfa753" check="intent" severity="high" paragraph="b12">Differs from our approved “Confidentiality obligations”: The approved clause imposes strict confidentiality obligations with no residual exception. The counterparty's clause 2.05 creates a broad carve-out allowing use of information retained in unaided memory, which undermines the confidentiality obligations in clause 2.01. (favours them)</finding>
<finding id="f-mvg3wmta523f04" check="standards" severity="warn" paragraph="b12">Wording to fix it: Our standard position is that no residuals clause is acceptable. This clause would allow the counterparty to use our confidential information outside the purpose of the Transaction, which is a significant risk.

<finding id="f-mvg3wxwre101a5" check="conflict" severity="high" paragraph="b12">Conflicts with another clause: Section 2.05 permits unrestricted use of residual knowledge, which undermines the confidentiality obligations in Section 2.01 that require the Receiving Party to hold Confidential Information in confidence and use it solely for the Transaction. This creates a conflict because residual knowledge may include Confidential Information, and Section 2.05 allows its use for any purpose, effectively overriding Section 2.01's restrictions.</finding>
<finding id="f-mvg3wxwrffcc25" check="language" severity="warn" paragraph="b12">Language: The term 'unaided memory' is not defined in the contract and is ambiguous. It is unclear whether it includes deliberate memorization or only incidental retention, and it is inconsistent with the defined term 'Confidential Information' because it allows use of information that may fall within that definition without restriction. Suggested: Clarify the scope of 'unaided memory' or remove the clause to avoid undermining the confidentiality protections.</finding>
</part>

<part id="part-mvg3vf2m5184c7" title="Section 3.01 – Term and survival">
<paragraph id="b14" number="Section 3.01">
<now>This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and remain in effect for three (3) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party on thirty (30) days' written notice. The Receiving Party's obligations with respect to Confidential Information shall survive for five (5) years after expiry or termination of this Agreement.</now>
</paragraph>
<finding id="f-mvg3wquc808c6c" check="intent" severity="high" paragraph="b14">Differs from our approved “Term and survival”: The approved clause has a 2-year term; the contract has a 3-year term. (favours them) The approved clause has a 3-year survival for all obligations; the contract has a 5-year survival for Confidential Information. (favours them) The approved clause protects trade secrets for as long as they remain trade secrets; the contract has no such perpetual protection for trade secrets. The approved clause has no termination for convenience; the contract allows either party to terminate on 30 days' notice.</finding>
<finding id="f-mvg3wquc44589d" check="standards" severity="warn" paragraph="b14">Wording to fix it: Aligns term with our 2-year standard, reduces survival to 3 years, and adds perpetual trade secret protection.
Suggested wording: This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and remain in effect for two (2) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party on thirty (30) days' written notice. The Receiving Party's obligations with respect to Confidential Information shall survive for three (3) years after expiry or termination of this Agreement, except that trade secrets shall be protected for as long as they remain trade secrets.</finding>
</part>

<part id="part-mvg3vf2m0d8661" title="Section 4.04 – Non-solicitation">
<paragraph id="b20" number="Section 4.04">
<now>For a period of twelve (12) months from the Effective Date, Company shall not, directly or indirectly, solicit for employment or hire any employee of Kestrel with whom Company had contact in connection with the Transaction, provided that general advertisements not targeted at Kestrel employees shall not breach this Section.</now>
</paragraph>
<finding id="f-mvg3x11h838ffb" check="intent" severity="warn" paragraph="b20">Differs from our approved “Subscription term and renewal”: The approved clause of-term is about subscription term and renewal, not non-solicitation. The closest approved clause is not relevant to this part.</finding>
<finding id="f-mvg3x11h5b55fa" check="standards" severity="warn" paragraph="b20">Wording to fix it: To meet the acceptable fallback for pb-non-solicit and pb-mutuality, the clause must be mutual and limited to staff directly involved. </part>

<part id="part-mvg3vf2m347543" title="Section 4.06 – Governing law and jurisdiction">
<paragraph id="b22" number="Section 4.06">
<now>This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflict of laws principles. Each Party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Wilmington, Delaware.</now>
</paragraph>
<finding id="f-mvg3x9v44061d1" check="intent" severity="high" paragraph="b22">Differs from our approved “Jurisdiction”: The approved clause gives exclusive jurisdiction to the courts of England and Wales. <finding id="f-mvg3x9v5b5809d" check="standards" severity="warn" paragraph="b22">Wording to fix it: To align with our standard governing law and jurisdiction position.

<paragraph id="b9" number="Section 2.02">

<part id="part-mvg6ko3w3d8e9f" title="Definition: Confidential Information">
<paragraph id="b4" number="Section 1.01">
<now>"Confidential Information" means any non-public information, in whatever form, disclosed by a Party (the "Disclosing Party") or its Representatives to the other Party (the "Receiving Party") or its Representatives, whether before or after the Effective Date, including technical, financial, commercial and product information, and any information marked as confidential or that a reasonable person would understand to be confidential.</now>
</paragraph>
<finding id="f-mvg6ksqv029b1d" check="standards" severity="warn" paragraph="b4">Wording to fix it: Aligns exactly with our approved clause, removing the slight differences in wording (e.g. 'any non-public information' vs 'all information of a confidential nature').
Suggested wording: "Confidential Information" means all information of a confidential nature disclosed by or on behalf of one party (the "Disclosing Party") to the other party (the "Receiving Party"), whether before or after the Effective Date, in any form, including business, technical, financial and product information, and any information that is marked as confidential or would reasonably be regarded as confidential.</finding>
</part>

<part id="part-mvg6ko3wdaf86b" title="Section 2.01 – Confidentiality obligations">
<paragraph id="b8" number="Section 2.01">
<now>The Receiving Party shall (a) hold the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information in confidence, (b) use it solely to evaluate and pursue the Transaction, and (c) disclose it only to those of its Representatives who need to know it for that purpose and who are under obligations of confidentiality at least as protective as this Agreement. The Receiving Party is responsible for any breach of this Agreement by its Representatives.</now>
</paragraph>
<finding id="f-mvg6kstu40a171" check="standards" severity="warn" paragraph="b8">Wording to fix it: The wording is substantively equivalent to our approved clause. The only difference is the broader definition of Representatives (which includes Affiliates, agents, consultants and financing sources). If we want to narrow it, we could replace 'Representatives' with 'employees, officers, professional advisers and subcontractors' and delete the reference to Affiliates, but that would require amending the definition in Section 1.02. Given the mutual nature and the fact that the disclosure is limited to those who need to know for the Transaction, this is acceptable.
Suggested wording: The Receiving Party shall (a) hold the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information in confidence, (b) use it solely to evaluate and pursue the Transaction, and (c) disclose it only to those of its Representatives who need to know it for that purpose and who are under obligations of confidentiality at least as protective as this Agreement. The Receiving Party is responsible for any breach of this Agreement by its Representatives.</finding>
</part>

<part id="part-mvg6ko3wb5ae24" title="Section 2.02 – Exclusions">
<paragraph id="b9" number="Section 2.02">
<now>The obligations in Section 2.01 do not apply to information that the Receiving Party can show (a) is or becomes generally available to the public other than through a breach of this Agreement, (b) was lawfully known to it before receipt from the Disclosing Party, (c) is received from a third party who is not under a duty of confidentiality, or (d) is independently developed without use of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.</now>
</paragraph>
<finding id="f-mvg6kstv54dc80" check="standards" severity="warn" paragraph="b9">Wording to fix it: Aligns the third-party exclusion with our approved wording, which is broader and more protective of the Receiving Party.
Suggested wording: The obligations in Section 2.01 do not apply to information that the Receiving Party can show (a) is or becomes generally available to the public other than through a breach of this Agreement, (b) was lawfully known to it before receipt from the Disclosing Party, (c) is lawfully received from a third party without restriction, or (d) is independently developed without use of the Disclosing Party's Confidential Information.</finding>
</part>

<part id="part-mvg6ko3wad1b0b" title="Section 2.05 – Residual knowledge">
<paragraph id="b12" number="Section 2.05">
<now>Nothing in this Agreement shall restrict either Party from using, for any purpose, any information retained in the unaided memory of its Representatives who had access to Confidential Information, including ideas, concepts, know-how and techniques contained therein.</now>
</paragraph>
<finding id="f-mvg6kswxde7712" check="intent" severity="high" paragraph="b12">Differs from our approved “Confidentiality obligations”: The approved clause imposes strict confidentiality obligations with no residual exception. The counterparty's clause 2.05 creates a broad carve-out allowing use of information retained in unaided memory, which undermines the confidentiality obligations in clause 2.01. (favours them)</finding>
<finding id="f-mvg6kswx8eeb5b" check="standards" severity="warn" paragraph="b12">Wording to fix it: Our standard position is that no residuals clause is acceptable. This clause would allow the counterparty to use our confidential information outside the purpose of the Transaction, which is a significant risk.
Suggested wording: Nothing in this Agreement shall restrict either Party from using, for any purpose, any information retained in the unaided memory of its Representatives who had access to Confidential Information, including ideas, concepts, know-how and techniques contained therein. → Section 2.05 shall be deleted in its entirety.</finding>
<finding id="f-mvg6ksyf593076" check="conflict" severity="high" paragraph="b12">Conflicts with another clause: Section 2.05 permits unrestricted use of residual knowledge, which undermines the confidentiality obligations in Section 2.01 that require the Receiving Party to hold Confidential Information in confidence and use it solely for the Transaction. This creates a conflict because residual knowledge may include Confidential Information, and Section 2.05 allows its use for any purpose, effectively overriding Section 2.01's restrictions.</finding>
<finding id="f-mvg6ksyfabb396" check="language" severity="warn" paragraph="b12">Language: The term 'unaided memory' is not defined in the contract and is ambiguous. It is unclear whether it includes deliberate memorization or only incidental retention, and it is inconsistent with the defined term 'Confidential Information' because it allows use of information that may fall within that definition without restriction. Suggested: Clarify the scope of 'unaided memory' or remove the clause to avoid undermining the confidentiality protections.</finding>
</part>

<part id="part-mvg6ko3w836df7" title="Section 3.01 – Term and survival">
<paragraph id="b14" number="Section 3.01">
<now>This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and remain in effect for three (3) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party on thirty (30) days' written notice. The Receiving Party's obligations with respect to Confidential Information shall survive for five (5) years after expiry or termination of this Agreement.</now>
</paragraph>

Suggested wording: This Agreement shall commence on the Effective Date and remain in effect for two (2) years, unless terminated earlier by either Party on thirty (30) days' written notice. The Receiving Party's obligations with respect to Confidential Information shall survive for three (3) years after expiry or termination of this Agreement, except that trade secrets shall be protected for as long as they remain trade secrets.</finding>
</part>

<part id="part-mvg6ko3w2773e3" title="Section 4.04 – Non-solicitation">
<paragraph id="b20" number="Section 4.04">
<now>For a period of twelve (12) months from the Effective Date, Company shall not, directly or indirectly, solicit for employment or hire any employee of Kestrel with whom Company had contact in connection with the Transaction, provided that general advertisements not targeted at Kestrel employees shall not breach this Section.</now>

<part id="part-mvg6ko3w844f40" title="Section 4.06 – Governing law and jurisdiction">

<now>This Agreement shall be governed by and construed in accordance with the laws of the State of Delaware, without regard to its conflict of laws principles. Each Party irrevocably submits to the exclusive jurisdiction of the state and federal courts located in Wilmington, Delaware.</now>
